advances: This is a lower corrected-cap bound for the decreasing affine frustum in the nontrivial centered-slope branch. The higher-dimensional upper endpoint scalar and the full two-law bound require a separate upper certificate.

proof:
Use 0f434bd2af4ec1b8 at the stated $a,d$ to obtain $s_*>1$. The centered Dirac law at that slope satisfies $2v_*-1\le e_*\le(2v_*-1)/v_*\le v_*\le1$ by 18e7bdf54588779d. Write $R=1+as_*$ and $t_*=p/R^d$. The centered endpoint identities of 607c120102a3d53f give $2p\le1+t_*$ and $2v_*-1=2pe_*-t_*$. Also $\kappa>0$.

For $0<s\le1$, Jensen's inequality for the uniform law on $[-s,s]$ gives $e(s)\ge1$. Whenever $e(s)\ge1$, including $s=0$, the lower dual follows from $v(s)\le1$. For $s>1$ write
$$
J(s)=2s e(s)=\frac{(1-a)^{1-d}-(1+as)^{1-d}}{a(d-1)}.
$$
The derivative is $J'(s)=(1+as)^{-d}$, so $J$ is strictly concave and $2s-J(s)$ strictly increasing. At $s=1$ the latter is negative by strict Jensen. It tends to infinity since $J$ is bounded. Thus the positive denominator domain is a terminal interval. There the derivative of $(1-v(s))/(1-e(s))=(s-1)/(2s-J(s))$ has numerator
$$
2-J(s)+(s-1)J'(s)\le2-J(1)<0.
$$
In particular if $e(s)<1$ and $s\le T$, then $e(T)<1$ and it suffices to prove the endpoint inequality at $T$.

For variable $S\ge s_*$ define the cross-multiplied endpoint residual by
$$
E(S)=2S[(1+e_*)(1-v(S))-(v_*+t(S))(1-e(S))]
=A S-(1+e_*)+(v_*+t(S))J(S)-2S t(S),
\qquad A=1+e_*-2v_*\ge0.
$$
Let $q=1+aS$ and $N(q)=aE((q-1)/a)$. Substituting $J(S)$ and $t(S)$ gives
$$
N(q)=Aq+\mathrm{const}+Bq^{-d}-Cq^{1-d}-Dq^{1-2d},
\quad
B=\frac{1-a}{d-1}+2p,\quad C=2p+\frac{v_*}{d-1},\quad D=\frac p{d-1}.
$$
Thus the sign of $N''(q)$ is the sign of
$$
G(q)=\frac{q^{2d+1}}dN''(q)
=(d+1)Bq^{d-1}-(d-1)Cq^d-2(2d-1)D,
\qquad G'(q)=(d-1)q^{d-2}[(d+1)B-dCq].
$$
We have $G(1)=((d+1)(1-a)-2(1-a)^d)/(d-1)-v_*\ge1-v_*\ge0$. Indeed, the concave function $(d+1)x-2x^d$ on $[(d-1)/d,1]$ equals $d-1$ at $1$. At $x=(d-1)/d$ its excess over $d-1$ is $x(1-2x^{d-1})\ge0$, since $(1+1/(d-1))^{d-1}\ge2$ by the binomial theorem. As $G$ first increases and then decreases on the positive axis and tends to $-\infty$, $N'$ is nondecreasing and then nonincreasing on $[R,\infty)$, allowing an empty first interval. Hence $N'(q)\ge\min\{N'(R),\lim_{x\to\infty}N'(x)\}$ there.

The limit is $A\ge0$. Since $J'(s_*)=t_*/p$ and $J(s_*)=2s_*e_*$,
$$
\begin{aligned}
N'(R)=E'(s_*)
&=A+(v_*+t_*)t_*/p-2t_*+2s_*t'(s_*)(e_*-1)\\
&=(1+t_*-2p)\left(e_*+\frac{t_*}{2p}\right)
  +2s_*t'(s_*)(e_*-1)\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
$$
The factorization substitutes $2v_*-1=2pe_*-t_*$, and the signs use $t'(s_*)<0$ and $e_*\le1$. The same centered identity gives $E(s_*)=2s_*e_*(1+t_*-2p)\ge0$. Therefore $N$ is nondecreasing on $[R,\infty)$ from a nonnegative value, proving $E(T)\ge0$. The endpoint reduction proves the bounded pointwise inequality.

For $s\le T$, apply 18e7bdf54588779d to the Dirac cone law and f4be2679c83c2fd1 to its frustum truncation. In that truncation fact the parameter called $a$ is the top radius $r(U)=(1-a)/(1+aT)$ here, so its cap loss is exactly $tV_0$, its volume is $V$, and its coarea is unchanged. Consequently $(P_f(s)-cC_f(s))/V_0=\kappa e(s)+1-v(s)-t$. The lower dual bounds this by $\kappa-t$ from below. At $\infty$, the corrected cap is $V/2\ge\gamma V$ by 607c120102a3d53f. For $T<s<\infty$ the two records are interpolated with weights $T/s$ and $1-T/s$ by f4be2679c83c2fd1. The inequality therefore holds for every slope and remains true on averaging.

statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and $0<a<1/d$. Put $H=(1-a)/a$, $r(z)=(H-z)/(H+1)$, $p=(1-a)^d$, $C_0=(1-a)^{d-1}$ and $V_0=(H+1)/d$. Use density $r(z)^{d-2}/2$ on the cone $-1\le z\le H$, $|x|\le r(z)$. For $s>0$ set
$$
e(s)=\frac1{2s}\int_{-s}^{\min(s,1)}(1-ab)^{-d}\,db,\qquad
v(s)=
\begin{cases}1,&s\le1,\\ (s+1)/(2s),&s\ge1,\end{cases}
$$
with $(e(0),v(0))=(1,1)$. Let $s_*>1$ be the unique positive zero of the cone section moment, or equivalently of $\partial_a e(s)$ at fixed $s$. Write $e_*=e(s_*)$, $v_*=v(s_*)$ and $t(S)=p/(1+aS)^d$. For every finite cutoff $T\ge s_*$ put $t=t(T)$ and $\kappa=(v_*+t)/(1+e_*)$. Then for all $0\le s\le T$,
$$
1-v(s)-\kappa(1-e(s))\ge0.
$$

For the frustum obtained by cutting the cone at $U=HT/(H+1+T)$, write $P_f(s)$ for the mass of $z+sx\ge0$ and $C_f(s)$ for the integral of the density over $z+sx=0$ against $d\mathcal H^1/\sqrt{1+s^2}$. Its volume is $V=(1-t)V_0$. Set $c=(p-\kappa)V_0/C_0$ and $\gamma=(\kappa-t)/(1-t)$. Then $(P_f(s)-cC_f(s))/V\ge\gamma$ for every $s\in[0,\infty]$, with endpoint record $(P_f(\infty),C_f(\infty))=(V/2,0)$. The same inequality holds for the averages under every probability law on $[0,\infty]$.
title: The all-dimensional affine-frustum lower pointwise dual
